SEARCH
Package neqsim.process.equipment.separator.entrainment

Interface EnhancedEntrainmentProvider

All Known Implementing Classes:
BuiltInSevenStageProvider, SpecCarryOverProvider, ZeroCarryOverProvider
public interface EnhancedEntrainmentProvider
Service Provider Interface (SPI) for pluggable entrainment / carry-over models in NeqSim. Implementations are discovered at runtime through ServiceLoader and selected on a Separator via Separator.setEntrainmentProvider(String).

Why this interface exists. NeqSim ships with a single open-source "built-in" entrainment model — the 7-stage physics-based chain documented in separator-entrainment-modeling.md. Some operators have additional, proprietary correlations (e.g. Equinor's π-number empirical equation derived from the EQN scrubber test database) that cannot be open-sourced because they embed vendor or test-rig data. This SPI allows such providers to be delivered as separate, signed JARs that depend on public NeqSim only at the SPI level — no fork, no patching, no public disclosure of the proprietary content. If a private provider JAR is on the classpath ServiceLoader discovers it automatically; if not, code that requested it gets a clear error.

Public / private split policy. The public NeqSim repo holds the maximum amount of structure that does not leak proprietary content: SPI interface, method signatures, result / applicability data classes, registry plumbing, and provider ids (the string "eqn-pi-v1" is public; the correlation behind it is not). Only the numerical implementation, model parameters, validity envelopes, vendor-tagged data and correctness tests live in the private repo. Public and private are kept architecturally aligned — same package layout, same class names where possible — so a maintainer reading the public source can see what approach (4) requires and returns without being able to reproduce how it computes.

Stability contract. This interface is API-stable. Existing methods will not change signature; new capabilities are added only as default methods so existing implementations (including private plug-ins) keep compiling against new public NeqSim releases without recompilation.

Implementer responsibilities. An implementation must:

  • return a globally unique, stable getId() (no spaces, no version number — version goes in getVersion())
  • be deterministic given the same Separator state — providers are called from the steady-state and transient solvers and must not mutate global state
  • fail fast through checkApplicability(Separator) when inputs are outside the validity envelope, rather than silently extrapolate
  • register through a META-INF/services/neqsim.process.equipment.separator.entrainment.EnhancedEntrainmentProvider file in its JAR so ServiceLoader picks it up

  • Method Details

    • getApiVersion

      default int getApiVersion()
      SPI revision implemented by this provider. The default is 1 — the revision that ships with the first public release of this interface. When the SPI gains semantic capabilities that an old provider cannot express, public NeqSim bumps CURRENT_API_VERSION and providers built against the new revision override this method to return the higher value. The EntrainmentProviderRegistry refuses providers that declare an api version higher than the core supports, so version mismatches fail loudly at registration rather than silently at runtime.

      Adding new default methods to this interface alone does not require an api-version bump — only changes that affect what a provider must compute or return.

      Returns:
      the SPI revision this provider was built against; the current public revision is EntrainmentProviderRegistry.CURRENT_API_VERSION

    • getId

      String getId()
      Returns the globally unique, stable identifier of this provider.

      Examples: "neqsim-7stage" (built-in), "eqn-pi-v1" (Equinor private plug-in v1), "eqn-pi-v2" (v2). The id is the argument to Separator.setEntrainmentProvider(String).

      Returns:
      the provider id, must be non-null and constant for the lifetime of the JVM

    • getVersion

      String getVersion()
      Returns the version string of this provider.

      Recommended format: semantic versioning, e.g. "1.0.0". The version is recorded on the EntrainmentResult so plant historians and reports can tag which method produced a number.

      Returns:
      the provider version, must be non-null

    • checkApplicability

      EntrainmentApplicability checkApplicability(Separator separator)
      Checks whether this provider's correlation is applicable to the supplied separator configuration.

      Implementations must inspect the geometry, internals selection and operating conditions of separator and report any input that falls outside their validity envelope. The aggregate applicability flag is true only if every input is in range.

      Parameters:
      separator - the separator whose entrainment is to be computed; must not be null
      Returns:
      an applicability report describing in/out of envelope status and per-input diagnostics; never null

    • compute

      EntrainmentResult compute(Separator separator)
      Computes the entrainment / carry-over result for the supplied separator.

      Implementations should call checkApplicability(Separator) internally and decide whether to throw, extrapolate with a widened confidence band, or return Double.NaN carry-over values when inputs are out of range. Whichever policy is chosen must be documented on the implementing class.

      Parameters:
      separator - the separator whose entrainment is to be computed; must not be null
      Returns:
      the computed entrainment result tagged with this provider's id and version; never null
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the provider cannot produce a result (e.g. missing required input, hard out-of-range failure, missing data file at runtime)
